rules.title: Security Deposit Law - maximum deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. A pet deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.key_value: one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent; yearly increase not to exceed 10% of the current security deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (unless the tenant opts in by written request).
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings; a tenant in such a dwelling may make the law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Prepaid rent counted as security deposit
rules.requirement: Prepaid funds held to secure future rents, including last month's rent, are part of the security deposit; at the inception of the lease the landlord may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent, including the deposit and first month's rent.
rules.key_value: two and one-half (2.5) times the monthly rent at lease inception
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.citation: Brownstone Arms v. Asher, 121 N.J. Super. 401 (1972); Reilly v. Weiss, 406 N.J. Super. 71 (2009)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease. That means the landlo rd may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease, this includes the security deposit and the first month’s rent.

rules.title: Security deposit held in trust in interest-bearing account
rules.requirement: Deposit money must be held in trust and not commingled; a landlord receiving deposits for ten or less units must deposit it in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan in an interest-bearing account, while landlords with 10 or more units may alternatively use an insured New Jersey-based money market fund or a variable-rate account.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law, other than seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere).
rules.exemptions: Security deposits for seasonal use or rental (not more than 125 consecutive days by a person having a permanent place of residence elsewhere); does not include housing for seasonal, temporary or migrant farm workers. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies may be criminally charged as a disorderly person and fined not less than $200 or imprisoned for not more than 30 days, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

rules.title: Payment of interest on security deposit
rules.requirement: Interest or earnings on the deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent on the lease renewal or anniversary, or on January 31 if the tenant has been given written notice.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the ren ewal or anniversary of the tenant’s lease or on January 31,  if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest payments will be paid on January 31 of each year (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 (c)).

rules.title: Security deposit notice requirements
rules.requirement: Within 30 days of receiving the deposit and at each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the institution's name and address, deposit amount, account type and interest rate; the landlord must also notify the tenant within 30 days of transferring the deposit to a new landlord or account.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: If the tenant does not receive proper notice or interest, the tenant may give written notice that the security money plus interest at 7% per annum be applied to rent; for missed annual notice or interest the landlord has 30 days to comply first, and the landlord may not demand an additional deposit afterward.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.

rules.title: Return of security deposit after termination
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after termination of a tenancy, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest less deductions by personal delivery, registered or certified mail, with an itemized list of any deductions sent by registered or certified mail. No deductions may be made from the deposit of a tenant who remains in possession.
rules.key_value: within 30 days after termination of tenancy
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: The court may award the tenant double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Return of security deposit upon displacement
rules.requirement: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation (when an official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified displacement longer than seven (7) days), the landlord must return the deposit, and within three (3) business days of notice must tell the tenant where it can be collected.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation in rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: Security deposit on sale or transfer of property
rules.requirement: When the property is sold or transferred, the new owner must obtain the deposit plus accrued interest from the former owner and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest and returning it.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law that are sold or transferred.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

rules.title: Penalty for withholding deposits of assisted tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a deposit made by or for a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 per offense.
rules.key_value: not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense
rules.coverage_text: Security deposits made by or on behalf of tenants who received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
rules.penalty: Civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense, collected under the Penalty Enforcement Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:58-12).
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any Stat e or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) - housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental housing based on protected characteristics, including source of lawful income.
rules.coverage_text: All landlord-tenant relationships, except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences and age-restricted housing as to familial status.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex (e.g. YMCA) and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.
rules.penalty: Monetary damages and possible requirement to rent the unit to the complainant; fines and penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).
rules.quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
